messages.content: Write an announcement telling customers that a service is moving to a new platform next quarter. Around 250 words.

**Subject: [Service Name] moves to [New Platform] on [Date]**

Hi [Name],

[Service Name] is moving to [New Platform] next quarter. Your account, your data, and your billing history transfer as they are. Nothing to re-enter, no approvals to chase again.

Why now: the current setup has run on [old stack] since [year], and we've run out of room to add to it. [New Platform] gives us space for [specific capability, e.g. per-project permissions and an audit log], which customers keep asking us for.

**What changes**

- Sign in at [new URL] starting [date]. The old address forwards for 12 months.
- Point API traffic at [new endpoint]. Your existing keys still work, and the current endpoint stays up until [sunset date].
- [Feature X] behaves differently now. [link] has the details.

**What stays the same**

Pricing, contract terms, support hours, and your data retention settings.

**The cutover**

Accounts move in batches beginning [date]. Yours falls in [window]. We'll remind you a week out, then again that morning. Access goes read-only for roughly [N] minutes while we switch you over. If that timing is bad, reply to this email and we'll put you in a different batch.

Afterward, if something looks wrong, write to [support address] with MIGRATION in the subject line. Those land in a separate queue staffed through [date].

[link] has the rest: API changes, full timeline, and the rollback plan.

— [Name], [Title]

---

Fill in the brackets. Two of them decide your ticket volume: the reason you're moving now, and the [Feature X] line. Vague answers there generate the support load.
Rewrite the text above. Keep the same length and the same purpose. Return only the rewritten text.
